chapter: Funeral customs, Pickwick band and later years
title: Trio at Petone's with pianist Walter and Walter's turn to religion
summary: Love describes his three-piece band with a pianist and a drummer that sounded like a full band, and how the pianist turned to Jehovah's Witness books and drinking.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Yeah, they play as well. Dolly plays piano, you know, she's swell piano. And she play bass violin too. Lawrence play piano, she play the bass. Lawrence is the cornet player and the trombone player. Donnie lived right around the block. Right around. That's what worried in that little woman about there, about to get away from me. He was a nice trombone player. He worked with me when I was in the WPA band. He split the band in two. He wouldn't let me in that band. You know when they first got up, they had about two hundred members. They had about fifteen band players. Used to come to Petone's place in the fifth world, athletic club. I was working there, me and Walter, DeCruz, the piano and the other big hard drum. You talk about a band, you ought to hear that band. Trombie, piano and drum. Play more music in six pieces. And we played everything. Joe's a theme. You know those pieces they call them, My Joe's a theme? The real, we had music for that. People used to come sit down and listen to that band and say I don't see how they can do that. One fellow come in one night and invite the band to come and have a drink with them to the bar. Me and Ellick went in there and Walter was on one side, me and Ellick on this side, you know. He'd say, call the rest of the fellas in. Come on. Give us all the cocktails. He'd say, why the rest of the band? He'd say, this is it, this is it. He'd say, me, you mean to say you three fellas play all that music I heard in that? He'd say that's the only band he got there. He'd say I got to see that. He'd come in there and sit down right by the bandstand. He had a little bandstand there about wide at that door there. Just big enough for me to sit on and the piano, you know, sitting this way. And me right by Walter and Ellick were right down on the floor. And people used to pass down there and that music, they'd come in there. It's the way Walter played that piano, you know. He had a heavy bass and a compliment. And when I lead he'd just make chords, you see. And I'd play about two chords and cut out. Then he'd play the piece on the piano, you know. The piano is a band by itself. When he'd go to playing like that, well instead of me setting up there and holding my lap, I'd grab my derby, you see, place the horn in the derby and make an off melody like what he was playing. And that made it sound like an alto sax, you see. And some chords he made that sound like a tenor or something like that. And you'd swear they had strings and everything in that band. And Ellick was a light drummer, you know. People would be dancing out in the street and they'd come inside, you know, and say, them three fellas there making that music, they'd say, yeah, I don't believe it. And they'd sit down to look after a while, the place would be full, people would come in and see who was playing. And they used to say, I don't see how they can do that. We couldn't see either, but we used to do it. After a while, there come Peter on some of them, they'd sit down and enjoy the stuff, listen out to us playing. And all at once Walter went crazy about this watchtower business. He had books, a gang of books on his arm going around selling them and a draft for him. He turned out to be a preacher one time. He forgot his music. He couldn't play an outfit to save your life, not like that. He wanted to play like Steve Lewis and a whole lot of other fellas, you know. And he couldn't do it. It wasn't in him to play that way. He had a nice style of playing. The only fella was doing that in the city. I used to love to play with him. He played soft and loud. Always had a job. When he got to studying that Jehovah's Witness, he'd come as to drinking whiskey. He drank so much that he started me off drinking. I used to see him enjoying himself so much, you know, until he'd get too bad and then I'd cut out. When he got to studying them books, why I didn't go with me, I pulled out from him. This fella used to be with him, Joe Rennie, you know the one. He's a bishop, man. Yeah, he's a big man.
Yeah, he's a bishop now. He wears a big black gun.
He's the one learning water, all that stuff. I jumped off the bus up on Jackson and dried one night and jumped right in his arms. He said, Lord, look at y'all. That's my hot friend, Charlie Love.
